binary_evidence.loop_prevention_source_verbatim: yield It(`A hook blocked the turn from ending ${Pc} consecutive times — overriding and ending turn. For Stop/SubagentStop hooks, check stop_hook_active in the input and return success while it's true. Set CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP to raise this limit.`,"warning") -- confirms stop_hook_active is real and that the harness's own documented intent is: a Stop/SubagentStop hook MUST return success (allow) whenever stop_hook_active is true; the harness itself enforces a hard consecutive-block cap (CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP) as a backstop even if a hook ignores this, so a misbehaving hook cannot truly infinite-loop the harness, but the intended/correct hook behavior is to respect the field directly.

conclusion_for_step_2: background_tasks is a first-party, harness-populated field that directly answers 'is there in-flight background work right now' at the exact moment Stop/SubagentStop fires -- it makes the transcript-derived Bash/BashOutput/Monitor heuristic architecture investigation.md and plan.md's Step 2 hypothesized (before this evidence existed) unnecessary. The hook script (Step 2) reads payload['background_tasks'] directly instead of parsing payload['transcript_path'] -- a simpler, more authoritative check than transcript-JSONL parsing would have been, and still grounded entirely in real captured field names, not guessed ones. Separately, this ticket's own investigation subagent's real transcript (subagents/agent-a9fe8f10e7d252632.jsonl, TCK-20260902 predecessor) already independently confirmed there is no 'BashOutput' tool in this installed harness -- the real polling tool used everywhere in this repo's history is named 'Monitor' -- corroborating that investigation.md's own 'BashOutput/Monitor' hedge should resolve to 'Monitor' alone.
